# FTDC and Log Tooling — Complete Architecture Guide

Full-Time Diagnostic Data Capture (FTDC) architecture and log parsing utilities (bsondump, mtools, ftdc-tools) for microsecond metric inspection in MongoDB.

## System Architecture & Invariants
- [HIGH] (core) FTDC captures periodic serverStatus, collStats, and system resource samples into zlib/snappy compressed BSON chunk files inside the diagnostic.data directory.
- [HIGH] (core) FTDC samples are recorded at 1-second intervals by default; metric deltas are run-length encoded across chunk arrays to maintain a compact footprint under 200MB.
- [HIGH] (patterns) Extracting serverStatus.wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions reveals read and write ticket exhaustion where available tickets drop to zero under burst workloads.
- [MEDIUM] (antipatterns) Attempting to parse multi-gigabyte raw FTDC folders with text-based tools without decompressing chunk headers causes corrupt metric sequence extraction.
- [HIGH] (troubleshooting) Symptom: FTDC files consuming all root partition space. Cause: diagnosticDataCollectionDirectorySizeMB set too high on constrained storage. Fix: Set lower storage cap via setParameter.

## Primary Sources & Citations
- MongoDB Parameters Reference: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters/ (docs)
- MongoDB FTDC Utils Library: https://github.com/mongodb/ftdc-utils (repo)
- WiredTiger Internals Documentation: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger-storage-engine/ (docs)
- bsondump Utility Reference: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/bsondump/ (docs)
